content: In France, prenatal and postnatal care is fully paid for in public hospitals through the social security system. Employed women are also given 16 weeks of maternity leave, with daily payments ranging from €9.29 ($10.94) to €84.90 ($100), depending on their previous earnings. During pregnancy and the period around childbirth, money is not more of a concern than at other times: households in hardship still struggle, but not more than before, while affluent households remain comfortable. But when it comes to support for the mother, little is provided. Paternity leave is only 11 days long, which is too short for recovery after giving birth. New mothers must handle the constant demands of caring for a baby while also trying to heal. They also have to find care for their child, even though state-backed options are not enough, especially around Paris. Costs vary widely. In day-care centers, lower-income households may pay about €1,000 ($1,177.59) a year, but there is only one spot for every eight children. As a result, many families turn to private help such as childminders or care at home. Any other questions?.
